text:
sre-oncall: alert: SLO p99 latency burn + 5xx fraction spike for hosted-infer-usw2 — triggered by timeout-detector (alert-id: slo-htimeout-453). Observed 5xx fraction 4.8% (baseline 0.6%) over last 10m.

pagerbot: [automated] Incident created: INC-2026-022, paging oncall. Runbook: check gateway logs, trace coverage, recent deploys.

maya: looking now. any deploys in the last 30m? which routes affected?

ben: quick query from logs (kql):
```
index=gateway_logs env=prod region=usw2 status>=500 | count() by upstream_service, status | sort -count | head 20
```
Result: upstream_service: hosted-infer-proxy (502: 340, 504: 120), auth-gateway: 502: 12. Spike concentrated on path: /v1/generate and /v1/stream.

ben: sampling traces for last 15m shows trace coverage dropped to ~18% (norm ~82%). lots of connection resets at envoy->batcher layer.

kai: I see a canary rollout for infer-batcher-v2 started ~22m ago (deployed by ci/cd). Canary set to 20% traffic. Could be flaky kernels on new instances.

maya: good catch. can we quickly confirm error typology? are these upstream errors (model runtime) or LB timeouts?

ben: stack snippet from gateway logs: 
```
2026-03-17T14:02:11Z ERROR proxy request failed: upstream reset by peer, code=502, conn_id=9345
2026-03-17T14:02:14Z WARN prefetch timeout after 12000ms route=/v1/generate req_id=xx
```
Suggests upstream resets + some long tail prefetch timeouts.

maya: any auth/billing anomalies? customer escalations pointing to 401/402?

ben: NO, auth requests stable. billing events nil. This is pure 5xx/timeouts.

kai: rolling canary artifacts: infer-batcher-v2 images use new libaio 0.4. Reproducer on staging showed increased handshake retries under bursty short requests. Maybe kernel tuning needed.

maya: plan: 1) pause canary routing (flip canary->0%) 2) enable fallback to infer-batcher-v1 for affected routes 3) increase envoy upstream keepalive and bump retry budget temporarily 4) collect fresh traces with higher sampling for 15m.

ben: executing log commands now to pause canary. patching traffic weighting via rollout service: `rollout set-weight infer-batcher-v2 0 --env prod --region usw2`

kai: done. rollout API returned success. confirming traffic shift...

pagerbot: [automated] Rollout event: infer-batcher-v2 weight changed to 0 by ben at 2026-03-17T14:18Z.

ben: re-running error query: 5xx fraction down to 1.1% in last 5m. p99 latency trending back down. trace coverage still low but we should get more traces now that fewer resets.

maya: good. open a follow-up ticket with infra/release to investigate batcher lib/kernel mismatch. assign to kai. Include reproducer and perf traces.

kai: creating ticket INFRA-8721 with logs and staging repro steps. note: staging had flaky kube node affinit y; will include pod-level netstat and kernel params.

maya: for root-cause timeline: canary started ~14:00, spike started ~14:05, canary paused 14:18, errors reduced by 14:25. Marking incident as mitigated.

ben: FYI added temporary alert tweak: increase detection threshold for host-level prefetch timeouts to avoid noisy alerts during rollback churn. Will revert after postmortem.

sre-oncall: thanks. Please paste the dashboard panels you used so support can reference them in the CS response.

ben: dashboard links: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/slo/hosted-infer-usw2 and query snippets saved under Observability -> Saved Queries -> "gateway_5xx_by_upstream_usw2"

maya: quick note for support response: apologetic, explain mitigation (paused canary + fallback), confirm no auth/billing impact, ETA for RCA ticket ~48h.

kai: adding more context in INFRA-8721: kernel's tcp_retries2 and netfilter conntrack limits seemed at default; under our short-lived connection pattern with new libaio we saw resets. Workaround: bump keepalive and reduce handshake timeout at proxy layer.

ben: marking thread for postmortem. will capture timeline and sample traces in the ticket.

pagerbot: [automated] Incident INC-2026-022 status changed to mitigated by maya.

maya: closing loop with support: cc @support-leads — we can tell affected users we mitigated and will follow up with RCA. Any objections to sending a short note now?

sre-oncall: go ahead. keep the RCA ticket open and tag eng-releases + infra.

ben: sending note to support now.

maya: thanks everyone. will follow up in INFRA-8721 with more trace analysis and a postmortem doc (link to be added).

ben: postmortem draft: causes = canary batcher kernel/kernel-user mismatch causing upstream resets -> cascade 502/504 at gateway; mitigation = paused canary, fallback to v1; action items = improve canary health checks, increase trace coverage, add synthetic probes for prefetch handshake timeouts.

kai: + add an automated rollback trigger when 5xx fraction >3% for 10m during any canary rollout.

sre-oncall: noted. closing thread after postmortem posted.

maya: thread archived for incident tracking.
